Team — looping you in to capture a concise set of asks from Horizon Bank and the auditor team so we can lock owners and timelines before the kickoff. High-level items below; please reply inline with owners/due dates. I attached an updated control-owner matrix (control-owner_matrix_v2.xlsx) and a short kickoff agenda.

1) Audit windows and sample sizes (FedRAMP) — Horizon asked for a proposed snapshot cadence for enclave snapshots and log sampling windows. Who will own the sampling methodology and the evidence extraction runbook? (owner / SLA)

2) ISO 27001 artifact readiness — specific ask: scope statement, Statement of Applicability (SoA) export, and latest internal audit findings. Do we have a single export point and versioned artifacts?

3) KMS and key rotation evidence — auditors often want rote proof of rotation and key usage. Can we produce KMS rotation logs for the last 12 months and HSM attestations if requested?

4) Live interviews / role-based questions — auditors may request 45–60 minute interviews for: control owners, SRE on incident response, and product security for design docs. Can we provide preferred interviewer names and available windows week of Nov 16?

5) Tracing and per-request IDs — Horizon asked whether we can provide request-level trace IDs and the policy for log retention/PRIV redaction (PII). Who owns runbook and can confirm extraction path?

Please keep replies tight. My ask: owners + one-line status + whether any new artifacts need creation before the kickoff (and estimated days).

Thanks,
Kimberly

Hi Kimberly — thanks for the clear list. A few clarifying points from our side before we finalize the kickoff agenda and sample requests: 

A) Snapshot cadence — For FedRAMP we require a minimum of one full enclave snapshot and a secondary differential snapshot within 30 days of the audit start. Can you confirm Redwood's ability to provide atomic snapshots and the typical time-to-produce (we see 4–8 hours in some vendors)? Also confirm whether snapshots include full KV cache dumps or only disk images.

B) Log retention and redaction policy — We need a short statement on how Redwood redacts PII in logs destined for auditors. If you can provide the policy doc or link, that helps. Also we expect a 90-day retention export for the control sample window.

C) Per-request trace IDs — auditors may ask for request->trace linking for 2–3 sampled requests. Please confirm that trace IDs are exposed and whether they map back to tenant-level metadata we can share.

D) Sampling methodology and sample size justification — Provide the statistical method you intend to use and expected sample size for control testing (prefer conservative numbers).

E) Interview roster — We'll aim for 3 interviews (control owner, SRE, product security). Please confirm names and availability Nov 16–18.

Finally, can we schedule a 30-minute pre-kickoff this week (Nov 9–11) just to validate the extraction paths and the places where we'll redact? Our audit lead, Maria (maria.lopez@horizonbank.com), is copied on this message.

Regards,
Luis Ortega
Head of Security Assessments
Horizon Bank

Luis / Maria — thanks for the quick review and the concrete asks. Answers and next steps below.

A) Snapshots — Marcus confirms we can produce an atomic enclave snapshot and a differential within the 30-day window. Typical time-to-produce: initial snapshot ~6 hours (depends on size); differential <60 minutes. Snapshots include disk images and metadata; KV cache dumps are available on request but treated as sensitive — we'll need an approved scope statement to include KV contents. Marcus: please prepare the snapshot runbook and an estimated production timeline (ETA Nov 10).

B) Log retention / redaction — We redact PII at export time via our redaction pipeline; policy doc linked here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cExample (internal redaction SOP). We can produce a 90-day retention export for the control sample. Tessa, confirm the redaction SOP version we will provide.

C) Trace IDs — We expose request-level trace IDs. Those map to tenant_id and request metadata; we can provide mappings with tenant-level fields removed if required. Marcus will provide the export format and a sample mapping (ETA Nov 10).

D) Sampling methodology — We will use stratified random sampling keyed by tenant and request type to ensure representative coverage; conservative sample size: 60 requests per control (subject to auditor acceptance). Rishi will share the sampling justification doc (SEC-547) by Nov 12.

E) Interviews — Confirmed interview roster:
- Control owner: Tessa Morgan (Compliance) — available Nov 16 AM
- SRE lead: Marcus Lin (Infra) — available Nov 16 PM
- Product security: Rishi Malhotra — available Nov 17 AM

Pre-kickoff — we can do 30 minutes on Nov 10 at 10:00 AM PT. Proposed agenda attached (audit-kickoff-agenda.pdf). Please confirm.
